```{r}
library(reactable)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
```

```{r}
#Find the three countries with the most universities on the above rankings.

df<- read.csv("http://manctsui.github.io/datasets/timesData.csv") 

top_three_country <- df |>
  select(country,world_rank) |>
  count(country, sort = TRUE) %>%
  rename(number_of_universities_on_rank_list = n) |>
  head(3) 

reactable(top_three_country)
  
```

```{r}
#Display the result of Problem 1A as a barchart in ggplot or plotly
plot_ly(data= top_three_country, x= ~country, y= ~number_of_universities_on_rank_list, type = "bar", color ="red")
```

```{r}
#Display the top 50 universities in the year 2011 as a table with only two columns:
Topfifty <- df |>
  filter(year == 2011 & world_rank %in% 1:50) |>
  select(world_rank, university_name)
reactable(Topfifty)
```

```{r}
#If we are to turn the data frame that results from Problem 1A as a SharedData object, would $rank column be a good candidate to use as a key? Explain.

# No, rank would not be a good candidate to use as a key since some values repeat and for it to be a key, the values must be unique. 
```

```{r}
#Create a filter slider from crosstalk that allows us to narrow our selection of universities based on the rank of the university

Based_on_Rank <- df |>
  mutate(world_rank_num = as.numeric(world_rank)) |>
  select(university_name,world_rank_num) 


sd<- SharedData$new(Based_on_Rank)
filter_slider("rank_slider", "World Rank", sd, ~world_rank_num)
reactable(sd)

```
```{r}
#Do two separate scatterplots from our university world ranking dataset restricted to the year 2016:
  #First scatterplot is number of students vs. student-staff ratio.
  #Second scatterplot is student-staff ratio vs. teaching score.
  #Link the two scatterplots together via crosstalk.

Yr2016Dataset <- df |>
  filter(year %in% 2016)

plot1 <- plot_ly(Yr2016Dataset, x= ~num_students, y= ~student_staff_ratio, type= "scatter")

plot1

plot2 <- plot_ly(Yr2016Dataset, x=~student_staff_ratio, y=~teaching, type ="scatter")
plot2

subplot(plot1,plot2) 
```
